topic: A person discovers their child has the same teacher they had
text: Well, I’ll be. When I heard Old Man Elric was teachin’ the lad, my heart took to a funny dance. I remember his lessons well, sharp as a hoe in the summer soil, never lettin’ us off easy. The way he’d make us recite the seasons, the saints, the turnin’ of the earth, till it felt like them words were carved right into my bones. Now, thinkin’ of my boy sittin’ under that same hard gaze, I can’t help but wonder if I did enough, if I taught him to stand tall when the wheat bends. I reckon I’ll have to visit the school, see how he’s farin’, maybe even catch a glint of my younger self in his eyes.
